Album / Artist: The Singer in My Band / This Is Lorelei

Label: Matador Records

Release Date: September 11, 2026

Review Date: 10/4/2026

Reviewer: DJ Stace

General Comments / Reviews:

Nate Amos gets in the car and comes back with a twangy alt-country road record. Tight, warm and catchy as hell. Look for cover versions of most of these, a la Box for Buddy, cause who could resist? - DJ Stace

Release Notes:

Third album from Nate Amos as This Is Lorelei, and his first for Matador.

Self-produced and recorded at his home studio in Brooklyn.

Amos calls it his road album; he wrote the songs daydreaming in the car with no instruments.

Lead single Billy Came Back (June 23, 2026). NACC #12 the week of Oct. 1.

released September 11, 2026

FCCs: None found

RIYL: MJ Lenderman, Wednesday, Alex G, Big Thief

Play: All, Favs Rated with up to *****

Tracklist:

1. *** I Will Eat My Heart in the Morning Light 03:18 - Upbeat guitar anthem. Great lyrics and vocals. Sourced: Called a stripped-down, emotional goodbye (Paste); Low register in the chorus nods to Stephin Merritt of the Magnetic Fields (Spectrum Culture).
2. ***** Oh No Now My 03:09 - Strong mid tempo thumper with great guitar hook throughout. Least alt-country track of the album. Stacked harmonies over low-tuned guitars. Play it!! Sourced: Heavily indebted to Alex G, darker and grungier (NME); Sounds like a different This Is Lorelei album, with heavier guitars (Northern Transmissions).
3. **** Billy Came Back 03:10 - Upbeat, jangly strummer about Billy, a karaoke legend. Sourced: Lead single. Uptempo yet melancholy, built on keys, drums and acoustic guitar (Americana Highways); Framed as immortalising a karaoke legend (Beats Per Minute).
4. *** Watching Heaven Fall 03:13 - Upbeat country popper. Sourced: Called jaunty and rootsy (NME); Upbeat bluegrass track with a scratchy fiddle pushed back in the mix (Exclaim!).
5. *** Sailing (Your Baby's Down) 03:33 - Medium tempo upbeat country harmony yacht rocker. Sourced: Electric guitar arpeggio in the vein of Jackson Browne and early Eagles in the verses (Exclaim!); Layers of harmony, gentler than the tracks before it (Song Bar).
6. *** The Singer in My Band 02:26 - Upbeat country rocker with banjos. Sourced: Amos's father, bluegrass musician Bob Amos, plays banjo, and his sister Sarah sings backing vocals (Paste); Called the rambling, country-flecked title track (NME).
7. Nitro 01:27 - Fast paced low tuned acoustic guitar instrumental. Sourced: Fingerstyle piece in an odd time signature (Paste); Brief instrumental of guitar and violin (Song Bar).
8. ***** Hey Sarah Is It Gonna Rain Forever 03:28 - Continuing the riff from the previous instrumental, becomes a cool baritone guitar stomper anthem to Sarah. Great vocal styling. Playing this one heavily on The Library Show. Sourced: Called the twangiest stretch in the Lorelei catalog (Paste); Soaring string arrangement (Archynewsy).
9. **** The Kid With the Crown 04:15 - Starts with a light acoustic guitar jam, abruptly hits with an alt-country rocker punch in the face, and stays upbeat and bright throughout. Sourced: Single with a video directed by Spencer Kelly, following kids cheering on a demolition derby racer (Alt Press); Called the country-fried hot rod of the album (Paste); Layered choruses inspired by Gordon Lightfoot's production (Sister Ray).
10. **** And I Haven't Seen My Love in Quite a While 03:29 - Fast-paced country two-step bouncer. Segue with Old 97’s. Sourced: Bluegrass song about jilted lovers (Paste); Built on baritone guitar, with a verse from Al Nardo, Amos's Water From Your Eyes bandmate (Americana Highways).
11. **** Don't You Cry in Lonesomeness 03:19 - Strumming electric guitar and vocals alone. Brief. Goes quiet at 3:05, and hangs dead air for about 15 seconds. Sourced: Closer slows everything down (NME); Strummed electric intro giving way to a promise of comfort (Americana Highways).
